name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: France–Bund spread 151.8bp on 13 Nov, just above 150bp but not sustained; US 10-year yield near 5.15% on 16 Nov
state: The France–Germany 10-year spread closed at 151.8bp on 13 Nov with French yields at 4.89%, up from 142.4bp on 10 Nov; it has swung either side of 150bp since peaking near 170bp in late October (Ideal Investisseur). The US 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.15% on 16 Nov (Motley Fool). With no sustained break above 150bp, failed G7 auction or emergency central-bank purchases found as of 16 Nov, Watch holds pending a sustained break.
for_you: Governments, mortgage borrowers and firms refinancing debt are exposed to higher borrowing costs as long-term yields rise. Holders of French and US government bonds are exposed to price falls.
rubric_hit: France–Bund 151.8bp at Alert line but not sustained; G7 yields at multi-year highs: Watch

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
